questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Singapore because of the nice weather, travel opportunities, and the high academic level at NUS.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy – NUS provided detailed guides for every step of the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn’t seek much assistance upon arrival. They have a well-organized system for new students. If I was ever in doubt, I just talked to the other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
NUS was very helpful – they responded quickly to any inquiries. 
I didn’t attend much of the orientation as I came a bit late to Singapore. I can highly recommend coming at least one week before school starts. It takes time to settle in, meet the other students + it is nice to get to know the city a bit before school starts.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The housing was ok. It was fine considering the price. I lived at PGPR and paid around 14.000 kr. for the entire period. Be aware that even though you can apply for a room with private bathroom, you will most likely have a room with shared bathroom and kitchen. However, it was not a big problem at all. I didn’t spend much time in my room during the days in anyways.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were some on-campus housings with meal plans (meaning that you get a meal served for breakfast and dinner). I would prefer living without meal plan. The food was often not very good, and I prefer choosing what I eat.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the deadline for on-campus housing! The most important one as there won't be a second round. Even though on-campus housing a bit out of the city, I will highly recommend applying. You will save a lot of money. And it is much easier meeting other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was very easy. Of course there were a lot of deadlines, but the guides from NUS made it easy. It takes some time, but don’t let that scare you.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process for courses consisted of several rounds. You begin the first registration round, before you come to Singapore. If you don’t get all the courses, you can apply again in the next round. The last round of registration is after the semester has begun. So you can even try out some courses, and then drop it again, if you don’t like it. Actually, I liked the system much more than the registration system at UCPH.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always contact the school if any doubt. They responded quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I missed the deadline for the first round, but it didn’t matter. I still got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice would be to try to keep up with the deadlines. But don’t stress out if you make a mistake. There is a lot of deadlines for everything, but in the end everyone just wants you to have a good exchange experience. There will always be help to find.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was very similar to what I know from UCPH, which was nice.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was mostly lecture style in classes of around 30 people. However, you get assessed on your participation. Therefore, it will also be interactive. That is different from UCPH. But don’t let it scare you. My experience was that the participation assessment was an opportunity for the students to drag their grades up. But it doesn’t affect your grade in a negative direction.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Criminal Law, International Environmental Law, Multinational Enterprises and International Law, International Space Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I can recommend all of my courses except the latter. Probably just because I didn’t find it interesting. 
However, I will recommend taking three 5-units courses and one intensive 4-unit course. With this combination you will have the workload spread out throughout the semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The room is very minimalistic. You have to buy hangers, pillow, and utensils for the kitchen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was more expensive than I thought. Therefore, you will mostly buy your food in food courts, which is cheap. It is manageable not spending enormous amounts of money on food, if you choose to go to the cheap places. The food courts are placed all around campus, so it is pretty easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The local students all attended a lot of different clubs and sports. It was a bit difficult figuring out what and how you could join. Several of the sports activities you had to sign up for in the very beginning of the semester. So keep an eye out for this!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The place, PGPR, where I lived arranged some activities – for instance a bike tour around the city during the night and yoga classes. The Law Faculty also hosted some lunches.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend signing up for sports activities. I regret missing the deadlines in the beginning of the semester. It’s a great way to meet people and especially also the local students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I will highly recommend exploring Singapore, as it is the city you now live in. Go to the tourist attractions and museums, do the Tree Top Hike and all the other stuff. But of course you also have a great opportunity to travel around Asia during the weekends and holidays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to adjust to the local culture, as it is a very well-functioning country. They have a lot of rules (also some weird ones), but it also makes it easy living there and safe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and don’t be afraid to talk to them. They might seem shy, but all of the locals I talked to, was really interested when we first started talking - even though there are so many exchangers each semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to accept that there will be more rules than you are used to. Especially, if you live on-campus, there will be rules about alcohol, visitors etc. But it is really not a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I found the culture a bit non-existing at times, because Singapore is one big mix of cultures. But that also made quite an interesting culture. 
I think especially their culture being affected by so many rules was what made it easy and safe living there.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.	Don’t stress out about the administrative work. Everything works out even though you make mistakes. Everyone wants to help you.
2.	Use the other exchange students from UCPH. They are probably doubting the same thing as you are. Or they are struggling with something similar, that they would like you help with.
3.	Don’t spend too much time studying. You will pass no matter what. Being on exchange is so unique. And there is so much more to do than studying.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun !!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Experiencing that you can make a home and an everyday life for yourself in another country. Meeting great people from all around the world. And of course, all the travelling!
Also, enjoying the time without job, family and friends. It made room for doing new things

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That it went by so fast :-) No major challenges.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No matter if you do a semester of exchange in Singapore or another place – just go! It might seem overwhelming, but the outcome makes it 100% worth it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
